table.name: battle
table.purpose: Catalog of battles between the Bulgarian Empire and the Latin Empire (Fourth Crusade era, c. 1205–1235), listing each battle's name, date, opposing commanders, and outcome. Other tables reference battles: ships lost in a battle (ship.lost_in_battle) and deaths caused by ships tied to a battle (death.caused_by_ship_id).

bulgarian_commander.name: bulgarian_commander
bulgarian_commander.description: Name of the commander leading the Bulgarian forces in the battle (e.g. Tsar Kaloyan, Boril, Ivan Asen II); 'Unknown' when not recorded.

date.name: date
date.description: Date of the battle, stored as free text with inconsistent precision (full day, month-year, or year only), e.g. '14 April 1205', 'June 1205', '1235'.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key identifying each battle; referenced by death.caused_by_ship_id and ship.lost_in_battle.

latin_commander.name: latin_commander
latin_commander.description: Name of the commander leading the Latin (Crusader/Latin Empire) forces in the battle, e.g. Emperor Baldwin I, Henry I, Boniface of Montferrat; 'Unknown' when not recorded.

name.name: name
name.description: Name of the battle or siege (e.g. Battle of Adrianople, Siege of Constantinople), unique per row.

result.name: result
result.description: Outcome of the battle: 'Bulgarian victory', 'Latin victory', or 'Two Year Truce'.

table.name: death
table.purpose: One row per recorded violent incident with casualty counts (killed, injured) and a location note. The data strongly resembles a casualty/incident register of attacks in Indian districts (e.g., Naxal insurgency), but the foreign key column joins equally well to two unrelated tables (battle, with medieval Bulgarian commanders, and ship, with naval dispositions), and the column name 'caused_by_ship_id' does not match the Indian-location content. The table's true domain and the referent of caused_by_ship_id cannot be determined from the evidence; the dataset appears internally inconsistent or assembled from mixed sources. The row-level meaning (an incident with killed/injured counts and a location) is clear, but the overall table subject is unresolved.

caused_by_ship_id.name: caused_by_ship_id
caused_by_ship_id.description: Foreign key to the event that caused the deaths/injuries. The name suggests it points to ship.id, and the join to ship.id is statistically accepted (ship lookup shows dispositions like Captured/Wrecked/Scuttled/Sank). However, a join to battle.id is equally accepted (battles with Bulgarian commanders Kaloyan, Boril, Ivan Asen II), which is semantically more plausible for a death/casualty table. The two candidate parents are inconsistent with each other, so the true target table is ambiguous; the column name alone is not reliable evidence.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key of the death table; unique integer identifier for each row (1-13).

injured.name: injured
injured.description: Count of people injured in the recorded incident; small non-negative integers, mostly 0 (11 of 13 rows), max 9.

killed.name: killed
killed.description: Count of people killed in the recorded incident; non-negative integers, mostly small (median 3), max 29.

note.name: note
note.description: Free-text note recording the location of the incident as 'district, state' — all values are Indian districts/states (Dantewada Chhattisgarh, Bastar, Bokaro Jharkhand, East Champaran Bihar, Gajapati Odisha, Kanker Chhattisgarh), consistent with Naxal/Maoist insurgency incident records. This conflicts with the battle/ship join lookups (Bulgarian medieval commanders, naval ship dispositions), so the table appears to mix data from different sources; the note column itself is clearly a location field.

table.name: ship
table.purpose: One row per ship lost (captured, sunk, scuttled, or wrecked) in a battle, recording the ship's name, type, tonnage, where it was lost, the battle it was lost in, and its final disposition. Ships are referenced by the death table (deaths caused by a ship).

disposition_of_ship.name: disposition_of_ship
disposition_of_ship.description: How the ship was lost: its final fate. Values are Captured, Sank, Scuttled, Wrecked.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key of the ship table; unique identifier for each ship. Referenced by death.caused_by_ship_id, indicating deaths attributed to a ship.

location.name: location
location.description: Geographic area where the ship was lost (e.g., English Channel, Mid-Atlantic, SW Approaches).

lost_in_battle.name: lost_in_battle
lost_in_battle.description: Foreign key to battle.id, identifying the battle in which the ship was lost. The battle table's lookup labels (Bulgarian commanders such as Kaloyan, Boril, Ivan Asen II) suggest the battle table covers medieval Bulgarian battles, which is inconsistent with these Napoleonic-era brigs — the join was accepted by LLM only, so treat the battle linkage as tentative.

name.name: name
name.description: Name of the ship (e.g., HMS Avon, Lettice, Mary).

ship_type.name: ship_type
ship_type.description: Rig/class of the vessel; all are brigs, some with gun count noted (18-gun Brig, 8 gun Brig).

tonnage.name: tonnage
tonnage.description: Intended to hold the ship's tonnage (numeric values 225, 391 present), but 5 of 7 rows contain the literal string 't' — likely a placeholder, unit marker, or data-entry error meaning unknown. The column is declared VARCHAR, mixing numbers and 't', so the meaning of the 't' rows is unresolved.
